artifacts.title: SMB null session to GPP creds and Kerberoasting (Active)
artifacts.starting_access: no credentials on a Windows Server 2008 R2 Active Directory domain controller
artifacts.outcome: domain Administrator via GPP credentials and Kerberoasting
transferable_properties: SMB null session shares are the first vector on AD machines with no credentials
the Replication share (SYSVOL copy) can contain GPOs with GPP credentials in Groups.xml
GPP Passwords (MS14-025) are cracked instantly with gpp-decrypt
a service account name containing TGS hints at Kerberoasting
use wmiexec.py on Windows 2008 when psexec has encoding issues
enumerate SPNs with GetUserSPNs.py as soon as you have any credentials

hypotheses.statement: anonymous SMB enumeration reveals share contents including GPP credentials

selected_action.intent: list SMB shares with a null session and inspect non-standard ones

evidence.summary: found the Replication share and retrieved Groups.xml containing a GPP cpassword for SVC_TGS

observations: GPP cpassword encrypted, decryptable with gpp-decrypt

hypotheses.statement: decrypting the GPP password yields service credentials usable for Kerberoasting

selected_action.intent: decrypt the GPP password with gpp-decrypt

evidence.summary: gpp-decrypt revealed the plaintext SVC_TGS password

observations: an SPN under the Administrator account exists

hypotheses.statement: Kerberoasting the Administrator SPN yields a crackable TGS-REP hash

selected_action.intent: run GetUserSPNs.py to request the Administrator SPN ticket and crack the hash

evidence.summary: obtained a TGS-REP hash for Administrator and cracked it with hashcat

observations: Kerberoasted credentials already belong to the domain Administrator

hypotheses.statement: the Administrator credentials give SYSTEM via wmiexec

selected_action.intent: get a shell with wmiexec.py as Administrator

evidence.summary: obtained NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM via wmiexec.py with the Administrator credentials
